newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY O/N RATES END A SHADE HIGHER AT 23 PCT.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY O/N RATES END A SHADE HIGHER AT 23 PCT.

text.p: - Hungarian overnight rates ended higher on Wednesday at around 23.00 percent from Tuesday's close of 22.75 percent, dealers said.
Traders said the rise had more to do with local market factors than Tuesday's quarter-point U.S. interest rate hike, which had been widely expected.
"There's interest in the market at the moment because the rates are higher than the repo rates," said Erika Kaiser of Budapest Bank. "We haven't seen any effect yet from the U.S. interest rate hike."
The central bank's one-week reverse repo facility currently stands at 21.00 percent.
Gabor Butor of Unicbank said that if anything he expected rates to drop a shade.
"The U.S. rate rise was already built into prices as everyone knew it was coming. Rates may slightly fall tomorrow," he said.
